item.question: A picture shows 9 children (practice values). 4 of them wear hats, 5 hold flags, and 2 of the children wear a hat and also hold a flag. True or false? (a): More than half of the children wear hats. (b): Some children wear a hat and hold a flag. (c): More children hold flags than wear hats.
steps: (a): The picture has 9 children. Half of 9 is 4 1/2, because 9 ÷ 2 is 4 with 1 left over.
(a): 4 children wear hats. 4 is less than 4 1/2, so it is not more than half. The statement is false.
(b): 2 children wear a hat and hold a flag. Some means at least one, and 2 is more than 0. The statement is true.
(c): 5 children hold flags and 4 wear hats. 5 > 4, so more children hold flags. The statement is true.
Check: 5 − 4 = 1, so exactly 1 more child holds a flag than wears a hat.
item.text:
Worked example: A picture shows 9 children (practice values). 4 of them wear hats, 5 hold flags, and 2 of the children wear a hat and also hold a flag. True or false? (a): More than half of the children wear hats. (b): Some children wear a hat and hold a flag. (c): More children hold flags than wear hats.
1. (a): The picture has 9 children. Half of 9 is 4 1/2, because 9 ÷ 2 is 4 with 1 left over.
2. (a): 4 children wear hats. 4 is less than 4 1/2, so it is not more than half. The statement is false.
3. (b): 2 children wear a hat and hold a flag. Some means at least one, and 2 is more than 0. The statement is true.
4. (c): 5 children hold flags and 4 wear hats. 5 > 4, so more children hold flags. The statement is true.
5. Check: 5 − 4 = 1, so exactly 1 more child holds a flag than wears a hat.
Answer: (a): False; (b): True; (c): True
